server-32gb-nvme.label: Target laptop - i5-10210U (4c/8t Comet Lake-U, AVX2, 15W), 32.6GB DDR4, NVMe, ~920GB free, Linux Mint XFCE
server-32gb-nvme.cpu: Intel Core i5-10210U @ 1.60GHz (turbo 4.2 single / ~3.x all-core, throttles at 15W)
server-32gb-nvme.dram_gbps_note: DDR4-2666 dual-channel = 42.7 theoretical x ~0.80 = 34. If the RAM is single-channel or 2400 this drops to 17-19 and EVERY row halves. VERIFY with roofline.py -- this is the number to check first.
server-32gb-nvme.disk_gbps_note: 10th-gen U-series has PCIe 3.0 only: NVMe caps at ~3.5 GB/s sequential, ~2.5-3 for large random reads. NOT the 5.5 Gen4 figure assumed earlier. VERIFY.
server-32gb-nvme.kernel_gbps_note: Taken from the CI runner (github-ubuntu-latest), which is ALSO 4 cores AVX2 and measured 21.9 fitted to 9.2 tok/s. Same core count and SIMD, so this is the best available number. Expect LOWER under sustained load: 15W U-series throttles hard after ~30s all-core; the runner does not.
server-32gb-nvme.os_reserve_note: XFCE + X11 is light (~1 GB); 3.5 leaves room for the browser you will inevitably open. Do NOT run a GPU driver-heavy desktop alongside.
server-32gb-nvme.gpu: Radeon 520/610 Mobile (2 GB GDDR5, GCN 1.0) -- too small and too old to help; -ngl 0 always. Do not build with HIP/Vulkan.
server-32gb-nvme.igpu: Intel UHD (CometLake-U GT2) -- shares system RAM; Vulkan backend possible but not worth it, it competes for the same DRAM bandwidth the CPU needs.

github-ubuntu-latest.label: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest (measured by CI run 31897530265)
github-ubuntu-latest.kernel_gbps_note: FITTED to the measured 9.2 tok/s on gpt-oss-20b (model fits RAM, so DRAM+kernel bound). 4 AVX2 threads, --no-repack. First real kernel number in this file.
